warning: CANONICAL PEAK-FCF SANITY-CHECK CASE (CLAUDE.md): an early run extrapolated the FY2025 record year (revenue $439.6m, EBITDA $95.9m, NPAT $32.0m, FCF $53.3m) and produced IV $22.75, implying 30x P/E and 3.4x P/B against a decade in which Seeka never traded above 0.99x P/B or 7.8x EV/EBITDA. This model is built on MID-CYCLE economics (year-2+ revenue ~$416m at 17-18.3% post-IFRS-16 EBITDA margin, ~$71-84m EBITDA) with the FY2026 guidance year as year 1, charges the IFRS-16 lease cash cost (~$20m/yr) inside the flows, and caps every terminal value at the stock's own historical EV/EBITDA range. Against FY2025/TTM peak earnings the implied multiples will sit at or below the historical floor; that is the expected relationship for a cyclical valued off normalised, lease-charged flows at a conservative 12% NZD discount rate, not a modelling error.

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: EPS and FCF CAGRs are not meaningful: FY2023 was a cyclone/frost trough (EPS -$0.34, FCF -$20.1m) and FY2020-2022 FCF alternates sign, so the maths is undefined or explosive (EPS 3-yr 68% is recovery off a $0.16 FY2022 base). Revenue (8-12%) and equity (3-11%) CAGRs span a trough-to-peak window. Growth was not selected by CAGR extrapolation; base-case revenue growth of 3-3.5%/yr from a mid-cycle year 2 reflects Zespri's five-year industry plan (+10% trays to 2030) without assuming the FY2025 record repeats. CAGRs are to FY2025 (FY0) and are unchanged from the prior build.
historical_growth.notes: SBC is negligible (<=0.05% of revenue every year) so the SBC-adjusted and reported FCF series are identical. The material historical distortion is cyclicality and expansion capex, not SBC: FY2015-2023 reported FCF is mostly negative because capex was orchard/packhouse growth investment, and FY2024-2025 FCF ($47.7m, $53.3m) are post-build-out record years. Reported FCF is also pre-lease (IFRS-16 principal sits in financing): FY2025 post-lease owner FCF is $34.6m.

scenario_narratives.base: Mid-cycle income-plus-modest-growth case: FY2026 delivered at raised guidance, revenue then moderates to ~$416m and the post-IFRS-16 EBITDA margin to 17%, recovering to 18.3% by FY2030 on SunGold mix and automation. Leases charged as an operating cost (~$20m/yr). Year-2 owner FCF ~$20m rising to ~$33m; terminal value is Gordon at 12%/2% (~4x EBITDA), below the 5.5x historical-average cap.
scenario_narratives.bull: Good 2027 crop, SunGold growth at the Zespri-plan pace, Australia scales, no weather event: revenue to $574m by FY2030 at 20-21% margins, owner FCF ~$60m. Value ~$8.6/share -- a re-rating to roughly the historical P/B ceiling (~1.1x book).
scenario_narratives.bear: Cyclone year in 2027 followed by a Zespri service-fee squeeze that leaves margins permanently below the FY2020-22 range. Equity is underwater on cash flows (EV below net bank debt); the bear is a balance-sheet survival case resolved by asset sales, dividend suspension or an equity raise rather than by the DCF.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Seeka is an income-plus-modest-growth holding, not a growth compounder: a fully imputed dividend (policy 50-75% of underlying NPAT; $0.30 paid for FY2025, $0.25 + $0.20 declared so far for FY2026, i.e. ~9% running yield at the current price in a strong year, ~5-6% at mid-cycle) plus mid-single-digit mid-cycle growth from SunGold mix and Zespri's industry volume plan, plus optionality from debt reduction. The house DCF values the mid-cycle, lease-charged flows at a conservative 12% and lands below the market price; the required-return table shows the current price corresponds to roughly a 10% discount rate on the same flows, which is a textbook NZ small-cap WACC. The stock trades at ~0.67x book and ~3.4x TTM EV/EBITDA (ex-lease), inside its ten-year range (P/B never above 0.99x, EV/EBITDA 3.1-7.9x), so the market is neither pricing peak earnings as permanent nor a cyclone as imminent.
valuation_philosophy.dividend_normalized_range: $0.25-0.35/share fully imputed, 50-75% of mid-cycle underlying NPAT (~$20-30m)
key_risks_to_valuation: Weather: a cyclone/frost year repeats FY2023 (EBITDA $26m, FCF -$20m) on a ~$120m net-debt, ~$83m lease balance sheet; the bear case is a negative-equity DCF.
Zespri single-desk dependency: ~60% of revenue; pool allocation or post-harvest fee changes hit Seeka with no substitutable customer.
Mid-cycle level: if FY2024-FY2026 (EBITDA $76m/$96m/~$88m) is the new normal rather than a run of good years, the 17-18.3% mid-cycle margin understates value by ~$1-1.5/share.
Seasonal net debt: the June balance sheet is the high point; December net debt is typically $15-25m lower (+$0.3-0.5/share not taken).
Lease growth: orchard lease liabilities rose $21m in 18 months; a lease charge held at 4.5% of revenue could prove light if leasing continues to fund expansion.
DRP dilution modelled at 1.75%/yr without crediting the retained cash (~$0.30/share conservative).

historical_multiples.note: FY-end (31 December) EV/EBITDA on ex-lease EV over post-IFRS-16 EBITDA (consistent with how the CSV and sanity check compute it); FY2023 is a trough-EBITDA outlier excluded from the average/max used for the exit caps. Carried over from the 2026-08-01 build.

scenario_cap_selection.rationale: Bear ~ 10-yr minimum region; base ~ ex-outlier average; bull ~ ex-outlier maximum (FY2017). Expressed to the engine as multiples of year-5 owner FCF (terminal_cap_multiple), none binding.

memo_prior_wacc_stack.note: What the preserved 2026-08-01 discount rates (14/15.5/17.5% with three stacked premiums) would give on the SAME lease-charged flows: base 2.03, bull 6.61, bear -1.36, weighted 2.33 NZD/share. That implies ~0.27x P/B and ~2.4x TTM EV/EBITDA, below anything the stock has traded at in a decade -- the premium stack double-charges risk once the lease cost and the scenario set are both in place, which is why the house rate was unified at 12%.

inputs.base_revenue_note: FY2025 (year to 31 Dec 2025) group revenue, FY0 for the growth path. FY2026 (year 1) is the guidance year: H1 2026 revenue $305.5m vs H1 2025 $307.9m; FY2026E ~$435m.
inputs.share_count_basis: Total shares issued 44,029,543 at 31 Dec 2025 (FY2025 AR note 18, includes ~1.78m held by employee/grower scheme trusts) plus H1 2026 issuance of $2.732m (DRP allotments and 2024 share schemes, statement of changes in equity) at the ~$4.7 DRP strike = ~0.57m shares, giving ~44.6m at 30 Jun 2026. The interim does not print an on-issue count; diluted EPS of $1.05 on $45.4m NPAT implies a 43.3m weighted diluted count ex trust-held shares. Held growing at 1.75%/yr (see annual_share_growth_pct); SBC is negligible so there is no SBC double-count.
inputs.share_growth_note: Genuine NON-SBC issuance, preserved from the 2026-08-01 build: the DRP applies to every dividend at a 2% VWAP discount (519,602 shares issued under the DRP in FY2025, ~0.57m in H1 2026, and a $0.20 dividend declared 19 Aug 2026 with the DRP applying). Run-rate DRP dilution 1.5-2.0%/yr; the $0.20 Oct-2026 and April-2027 dividends will add ~0.4m shares each. This is conservative: DRP cash is retained (reducing net debt) but is not credited in the flows, so the ~8% five-year count growth is a ~$0.30/share haircut on the base case.
inputs.net_debt_note: 30 Jun 2026 interim (note 12): interest-bearing liabilities $26.576m current + $96.619m non-current = $123.195m, cash $3.355m, net bank debt $119.8m (company's own NetBankDebt KPI 119.8). Lease liabilities of $83.362m EXCLUDED under lease treatment (B). June is the seasonal high point of Seeka's debt cycle (Dec-24 $137.3m -> Jun-25 $130.6m -> Dec-25 $100.3m -> Jun-26 $119.8m); the December 2026 figure will likely be $15-25m lower, which is worth ~$0.3-0.5/share and is deliberately not anticipated. The $0.20 dividend paid 15 Oct 2026 (~$9m gross, part DRP) is also after this balance date.
inputs.interest_income_note: FY2025 interest income $0.336m not stripped: Seeka is a net-debt company (net bank debt ~$120m), so there is no cash pile to double-count.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 cash flow statement share-based payment line $0.073m (CSV StockBasedComp), EquityAwardTaxes 0 in every period; SBC has never exceeded 0.05% of revenue (FY2015-H1 2026).
inputs.owner_fcf_note: last_fcf follows the contract (reported FCF less SBC less interest income = $53.2m) but is a PEAK-year figure and is pre-lease. Under lease treatment (B) the comparable FY2025 flow is $53.228m less lease principal $12.158m less lease interest $6.515m = $34.6m; the base-case year-1 (FY2026 guidance year) owner FCF of $37.0m and the mid-cycle year-2 figure of $20.4m should be read against that, not against $53.2m.
inputs.wacc_rationale: 12.0% in NZD, single rate across all three scenarios (risk charged once, in the flows). Built from the flows' own currency: NZ 10-year government bond ~4.5%, NZ equity risk premium ~6%, beta ~1.1 for a small-cap horticultural processor gives a cost of equity of ~11%; a 1-1.5pp size/illiquidity premium for a ~NZ$225m NZX small cap takes it to 12-12.5%; blending with ~35% market-value debt at ~6.5% pre-tax would give a textbook WACC of ~9.5-10%. The house rate of 12% is therefore an all-equity small-cap cost of equity applied as the WACC, i.e. deliberately conservative, and it coincides with the top of the 11-12% NZ small-cap base the 2026-08-01 build itself cited before stacking premiums. METHODOLOGY CHANGE vs the prior build, which stacked three ad-hoc premiums (Zespri single-desk concentration +1.5-2pp, weather cyclicality +1-1.5pp, illiquidity +1.5-2pp) to 15.5% and used 14%/17.5% on bull/bear. Those risks are now carried where owner-fcf-adaptations.md section (f) says they belong: in the scenario set (a cyclone-plus-Zespri-squeeze bear at 25% weight) rather than in the discount rate, and the premium stack is no longer needed to pass the historical-multiples sanity gate once the lease cost is charged (the stack had been doing the lease cost's job: see reconciliation). The required_return_table shows the market price corresponds to roughly a 10% rate on these flows.
inputs.lease_treatment: (B) leases as operating cost, chosen 2026-11-02. Lease cash cost (principal + interest, both read off the cash-flow statement: FY2025 principal $12.158m + lease interest paid $6.515m = $18.7m = 4.25% of revenue; H1 2026 $6.793m + $3.442m = $10.2m) is charged inside EBIT via lease_cost_pct_path, D&A is ex right-of-use depreciation (FY2025 depreciation $17.7m + amortisation $0.3m = 4.1% of revenue; H1 2026 annualised 4.3%), and lease liabilities ($83.4m at 30 Jun 2026) are EXCLUDED from net debt. Lease liabilities have been rising (Dec-24 $62.6m -> Dec-25 $81.7m -> Jun-26 $83.4m) as Seeka takes on orchard leases, so the charge is held at 4.5-4.7% of revenue rather than allowed to shrink. The 2026-08-01 build charged NEITHER (lease liabilities out of net debt, no lease cash cost in the flows, D&A at 7% including ROU depreciation) -- the error both method files name -- and this correction is the single largest item in the reconciliation bridge (-$2.81/share weighted).
inputs.nci_treatment: none: no material non-controlling interest; all flows attributable.
inputs.working_capital_note: wc_capture_pct +12% preserved from the prior build (unchanged). The method's sign rule would argue for a negative capture on a receivables-heavy processor; the effect is small (year-2 revenue decline costs $2.3m, growth years release $1.6-1.8m) and is left for the next full review rather than re-judged here.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF component DCF (SKILL.md row 'operating company, non-US or cyclical' -> owner-fcf.md + owner-fcf-adaptations.md: NZD build, IFRS-16 leases, SBC-zero market, cyclical risk charged once). Seeka is an operating post-harvest/orcharding business, not a REIT or LIC, so no other route applies. UPDATE of the 2026-08-01 hand-built DCF, migrated to the Drivers/engine route: the mid-cycle framing, 5-year horizon, year-2+ revenue levels and margin paths, capex paths, cash-tax ramps, DRP share growth, EV/EBITDA exit caps (3.5/5.5/7.9x), scenario weights (25/50/25) and narratives are preserved; the FY2026 guidance year is re-judged on the H1 2026 interim and raised guidance; anchors refreshed to 30 Jun 2026; two deliberate methodology corrections (lease treatment, single WACC) are stated above and bridged in reconciliation. SBC-zero market: house and street coincide, band_position is null by construction. Price is a regular-session NZX print (Monday 2 Nov 2026 10:36 NZDT), not after-hours.
unchanged_assumptions: Mid-cycle base: year-2 revenue $416m at 17.0% post-IFRS-16 EBITDA margin rising to 18.3% by year 5 (EBITDA $71m -> $84m), unchanged. Would move on: a second consecutive >=20% margin year in FY2027 on normal volumes (management attributes the H1 2026 margin lift on lower volumes to automation), or Zespri's 2027 crop forecast; the FY2023-FY2026E four-year average EBITDA of ~$72m supports the level as it stands.

Capex paths (base 5.9% -> 5.0% of revenue; FY2025 PPE capex $21.1m = 4.8%, H1 2026 $16.4m) unchanged. Would move on: an announced capacity expansion (the interim says the company 'is considering future capacity and growth opportunities').

Cash-tax ramps (base 10% -> 21%) unchanged; H1 2026 cash tax paid was $9k, consistent with the low year-1 rate. Would move on: exhaustion of FY2023 loss carry-forwards visible in a >20% cash rate in FY2027.
Scenario weights 25/50/25 and the bull/bear narratives unchanged (see weights_rationale).
Terminal growth 2.0/2.5/1.5% and EV/EBITDA caps 5.5/7.9/3.5x (historical ex-outlier average/max/min) unchanged; none binds (Gordon bound in all three).

bear.terminal_cap_note: 18.9x year-5 owner FCF = 3.5x year-5 EBITDA ($56.1m), the historical minimum region; Gordon (9.7x FCF) binds. The bear equity value is NEGATIVE: EV $84m against $120m net bank debt.
bear.narrative: FY2026 closes at the bottom of guidance ($432m, 19.5%), then a Cyclone Gabrielle-scale weather event hits the 2027 season: revenue -13.6% (the actual FY2022->FY2023 decline) with the post-IFRS-16 margin at 9.0% (FY2023 actual 8.6%), which with a fixed ~$20m lease bill means negative EBIT and owner FCF of about -$18m (FY2023 actual reported FCF -$20.1m). Recovery is then capped by ongoing Zespri pricing pressure on post-harvest service fees: margins settle at 12-13.5%, below the pre-SunGold FY2020-2022 range, with volumes growing only 2.5-5%. On these flows the equity is worth nothing on a five-year DCF -- the bank debt (~$120m) plus leases (~$83m) absorb the enterprise value -- and the floor becomes the asset backing (NTA $6.31/share at Dec-2025, orchards and packhouses at cost), as in FY2023 when the dividend was suspended for two years and net debt peaked at $172m.

base.terminal_cap_note: 14.1x year-5 owner FCF = 5.5x year-5 post-IFRS-16 EBITDA ($84.0m), the historical ex-outlier average EV/EBITDA; Gordon (10.2x FCF, ~4.0x EBITDA) binds.
base.narrative: Year 1 is FY2026 at guidance: revenue ~$435m (H1 $305.5m, H2 seasonally small), EBITDA margin 20.3% (~$88m; H1 actual $86.3m plus a thin H2 consistent with raised NPBT guidance of $39-43m against $47.5m in FY2025, implying a larger seasonal H2 loss). Year 2 resets to the prior build's mid-cycle: revenue moderates to $416m (-4.3%) and the post-IFRS-16 EBITDA margin to 17.0%, below FY2024 (18.5%) and FY2025 (21.8%) and above the FY2015-2022 range, then grows 3-3.5%/yr with the margin improving to 18.3% on SunGold mix and automation (Reemoon). Lease cash cost 4.5-4.7% of revenue, D&A ex-ROU 4.2%, capex normalising 5.9% -> 5.0%, cash tax ramping 10% -> 21% as FY2023 losses are used.

bull.terminal_cap_note: 16.0x year-5 owner FCF = 7.9x year-5 EBITDA ($120.6m), the historical ex-outlier maximum (FY2017); Gordon (10.8x FCF) binds.
bull.narrative: FY2026 lands at the top of guidance ($440m, 21.0% margin), then the good 2026 winter chill delivers a large 2027 crop and SunGold volume growth continues at the industry-leading pace (Zespri plan: SunGold +17% to 163.5m trays by 2030) while the Australian orchards finally scale as plantings mature, with no material weather event across the horizon. Revenue compounds 6-7.5%/yr to $574m with the post-IFRS-16 margin holding 19.5-21%; lease cost falls as a share of revenue on operating leverage.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 14.1x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Preserved from the prior build. Bear held at 25% (above the 15% house default) because a single weather event can take EBITDA from $96m to $26m inside two years (FY2025 vs FY2023) on a fixed-cost, lease-heavy, ~$120m-net-debt balance sheet, and ~60% of revenue runs through Zespri's single-desk mandate; the bear now carries a negative equity value, which is why its weight matters. Bull held at 25% because it needs three independent things (a good 2027 crop, Australia scaling, no weather event over five years) to go right. Base 50%.
probability_weighted.band_note: House and street coincide (SBC immaterial): the band collapsed, so band_position is null rather than a degenerate 0.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
